questions.question: Explain the difference between crime and deviance, and why deviance is socially constructed.

points.text: Crime = breaks the law (punishable by state). Deviance = breaks social norms (not necessarily illegal). Deviance is socially constructed because definitions vary across cultures and time (e.g. homosexuality was criminal until 1967). Becker: deviance depends on who defines it, not the act itself.

questions.question: Describe the differences between formal and informal social control, giving examples of each.

points.text: Formal social control: police (enforce law), courts (try cases), prisons (punish and rehabilitate). Based on written law with formal sanctions. Informal social control: family (socialise children), peers (pressure to conform), community (gossip, shame). Based on unwritten norms with informal sanctions. Both are necessary for social order but serve different functions.

questions.question: Evaluate whether the law operates equally for all social groups.

points.text: Marxist view: laws protect ruling class interests (property laws, low taxes for wealthy). Selective enforcement: police focus on street crime not white-collar crime.
